messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic (DMF) Platform for Chemiluminescent Detection of Rubella Virus (RV) IgG and IgM by Indirect ELISA

REAGENTS USED:
  - RV-Coated Paramagnetic Particle Suspension (virus-immobilized magnetic microparticles for antigen capture, 1.8 uL droplets)
  - Patient Sample (serum or plasma, pre-diluted, containing RV IgG and/or RV IgM, 1.8 uL droplets)
  - DMF-Compatible Wash Buffer (1.8 uL droplets, used in 4x wash cycles after each binding step)
  - HRP-Conjugated Goat Anti-Human IgG (detection conjugate for the RV IgG assay, 1.8 uL droplets)
  - HRP-Conjugated Goat Anti-Human IgM (detection conjugate for the RV IgM assay, 1.8 uL droplets)
  - Goat Anti-Human IgG Pretreatment Reagent (blocks endogenous RV IgG/rheumatoid-factor IgM interference before the IgM assay, 0.9 uL droplets)
  - Hydrogen Peroxide, H2O2 (chemiluminescent substrate component, 0.9 uL droplets)
  - Luminol-Enhancer Solution (chemiluminescent substrate component, 0.9 uL droplets)

STEPS:
RV IgG Immunoassay (7-step indirect ELISA):
1. Dispense a droplet of RV-coated paramagnetic particle suspension (1.8 uL) and separate the particles from the storage diluent.
2. Dispense a sample droplet (1.8 uL), deliver it to the particles, mix for 3 min, then magnetically separate particles from the supernatant.
3. Wash the particles in 4 successive 1.8 uL wash-buffer droplets, mixing and then separating from the supernatant each time.
4. Dispense a droplet of HRP-conjugated anti-human IgG (1.8 uL), deliver to the particles, and mix for 2 min.
5. Repeat the 4x wash cycle from step 3.
6. Dispense one droplet each of H2O2 (0.9 uL) and luminol-enhancer solution (0.9 uL), merge them with the particles, and mix for 2 min.
7. Measure the mean chemiluminescent signal over 10 s with the integrated photomultiplier tube (PMT).

RV IgM Immunoassay (identical 7-step assay, preceded by an IgG-blocking pretreatment):
0. Pretreatment: Mix a 1.8 uL sample droplet with a 0.9 uL droplet of goat anti-human IgG pretreatment reagent for 7 min to block endogenous RV IgG and rheumatoid-factor IgM before analysis.
1-7. Repeat the same capture -> 4x wash -> conjugate (HRP-anti-human IgM in place of anti-IgG) -> 4x wash -> substrate -> PMT-detect sequence described above.

INTERPRETATION: Results are reported as a signal-to-cutoff (s/co) ratio, calculated by normalizing the mean chemiluminescent signal of each assay to the mean signal of the corresponding cutoff control (a 10 IU/mL RV IgG calibrator for the IgG assay; the RV IgM cutoff Cal 1 reagent for the IgM assay). An s/co >= 1 is interpreted as positive; an s/co in the gray zone (0.69-0.99 for IgG, 0.75-0.99 for IgM) is interpreted as equivocal; an s/co below the gray zone is interpreted as negative. Diagnostic sensitivity and specificity of 100%/100% for both RV IgG and RV IgM were obtained against a commercial mixed-titer performance panel referenced against an Abbott EIA platform, supporting use of the method as a portable, decentralized alternative to central-laboratory rubella serology for identifying pregnant women at risk of transmitting rubella to their offspring.

sources.title: Digital Microfluidic Platform for the Detection of Rubella Infection and Immunity: A Proof of Concept

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's 7-step RV IgG indirect-ELISA protocol (Methods, 'RV IgG Immunoassay') and the parallel RV IgM protocol with its added IgG-blocking pretreatment step (Methods, 'RV IgM Immunoassay'). Both branches share the same capture -> 4x-wash -> conjugate -> 4x-wash -> substrate -> PMT-read structure, modeled as two sequential blocks in one script since BioScript has no notion of running assays in parallel on separate electrodes as the paper's 4-way aliquoting scheme does. Because the paper's detection modality is chemiluminescence read by an integrated PMT (relative light units), not a fluorogenic signal, the 'detect fluorescence' primitive is used as a stand-in for the generic detect-and-quantify step, representing the RLU chemiluminescent read rather than an actual fluorescence measurement, since BioScript's grammar does not expose a dedicated chemiluminescence detect module. The paper's diagnostic interpretation bands (positive / equivocal / negative s/co zones) are collapsed into a single if/else branch per assay using the two-level (positive/negative) numeric cutoffs (10 IU/mL for IgG, s/co = 1 for IgM), since BioScript's grammar does not support a 3-way equivocal band without additional nested conditionals.

numeric_mismatches.field: igg_signal = detect fluorescence / igm_signal = detect fluorescence
numeric_mismatches.note: Detection in the paper is integrated-PMT chemiluminescence (relative light units), not a fluorogenic assay. 'fluorescence' is used only because it is the sole detect module exposed by BioScript's grammar; it stands in for the generic RLU chemiluminescent read, not an actual fluorescence measurement.

The paper defines three interpretation bands per assay (positive / equivocal gray-zone / negative s/co thresholds); this is collapsed to a two-way if/else using only the positive-cutoff boundary, since a three-way banded interpretation would require nested conditionals not exercised here.

The paper's instrument runs 4 parallel replicate assays per sample by aliquoting reagents across 4 sets of electrodes simultaneously; BioScript has no primitive for concurrent/parallel electrode operations, so the script models a single serial assay per antibody class rather than 4-way replication.

numeric_mismatches.field: on-chip serial dilution (Supplemental Fig. 2) and off-chip RF IgM ELISA screening
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper's droplet-splitting dilution series and the separate off-chip RF IgM absorbance ELISA used to characterize calibrator cross-reactivity are not modeled, since BioScript has no droplet-splitting primitive and no external-plate-reader detect module.
